findings.label: Dermal interlacing smooth muscle bundles
findings.evidence: well-circumscribed dermal proliferation of intersecting fascicles of smooth muscle

panels.rationale: Single low-power H&E image of excised lesion showing well-circumscribed dermal smooth muscle proliferation of intersecting fascicles, confirming piloleiomyoma in patient with multiple painful piloleiomyomas evaluated for Reed syndrome.
panels.attribution_text: Kogan et al. Multiple Painful Papules on the Arm: A Clue to Reed Syndrome.. Cureus 2026. doi:10.7759/cureus.112648. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Low-power hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) demonstrated a well-circumscribed dermal proliferation of intersecting fascicles of smooth muscle.
in_text_mentions: Histopathologic examination of the excised lesion demonstrated a well-circumscribed dermal smooth muscle proliferation composed of intersecting fascicles, confirming the diagnosis of piloleiomyoma (Figures 3-4). Given the presence of multiple painful piloleiomyomas, the patient was subsequently counseled regarding the possibility of Reed syndrome and the importance of renal surveillance. A renal ultrasound was recommended as part of the initial evaluation.

At follow-up, the patient reported complete resolution of pain and tenderness at the excision site. Histopathologic evaluation confirmed a benign piloleiomyoma without evidence of malignancy (Figures 3-4). Renal function testing was within normal limits, and renal ultrasound demonstrated no evidence of renal masses. Although these findings are reassuring, a normal renal ultrasound does not exclude HLRCC, and continued surveillance with consideration of genetic evaluation and appropriate renal imaging was recommended.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (a, b, c, d, e). a: Low-power H&E of excised lesion from isolated piloleiomyoma case; caption describes interlacing spindle cell fascicles matching vocabulary histology finding. b: High-power H&E of same piloleiomyoma showing spindle tumor cells in fascicular proliferation. c: SMA IHC of same lesion with strong diffuse positivity, specific smooth-muscle immunoreactivity supporting piloleiomyoma. d: IHC panel of same piloleiomyoma lesion; fascicular spindle-cell morphology visible in background, with captioned focal CK AE1/AE3 positivity recorded as proposed finding since not in vocabulary. e: IHC panel of same piloleiomyoma lesion; underlying spindle-cell proliferation visible, with captioned heterogeneous focal CD34 positivity recorded as proposed finding.
panels.attribution_text: Lazouzi et al. Isolated Piloleiomyoma Presenting as a Keloid Scar: A Case Report.. Cureus 2025. doi:10.7759/cureus.88546. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 2.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathological and immunohistochemical features of the lesion (a) Low-power magnification (H&E stain, ×40) showing a dermohypodermal proliferation composed of interlacing fascicles of spindle cells. (b) High-power view (H&E stain, ×400) revealing spindle-shaped tumor cells with elongated, moderately atypical nuclei and visible mitotic figures (white arrow). (c) Strong and diffuse cytoplasmic expression of anti-smooth muscle actin in tumor cells (green arrow). (d) Focal cytoplasmic positivity for cytokeratin AE1/AE3 (blue arrow). (e) Heterogeneous and focal membranous expression of CD34 (orange arrow).
in_text_mentions: There were no other similar lesions or palpable lymphadenopathy. A surgical excision of the lesion with histological study revealed a dermohypodermal spindle cell tumor proliferation, expressing on immunohistochemical analysis anti-smooth muscle actin antibodies, desmin, and PS100 in a heterogeneous manner, focally CD34 and CK without expression of CD68 (Figure 2).
